Vision Pattern Recognition, pp. 225–232, 2011. same central processing unit (CPU) within the system in order to avoid a data transfer over the slower Intel QuickPath Interconnect (QPI) between CPUs in current Non-Uniform Memory Architecture (NUMA) system architectures. For this reason, we utilized a single CPU system. Display We support a variety of target displays in our stitching pipeline. These include a regular 4K computer display, an HMD, and a Pufferfish display. Computer Display In the case of a standard 16:9 4K computer display, the panorama resulting from the video stitching operation is texture mapped onto the inside of a sphere. The viewer is placed into the center of the sphere with a 180° field of view projected onto the flat computer display. This method was used to validate our implementation and to permit different people to view our realtime results. HMD The stitched panorama was also rendered for an Oculus VR headset using the OpenVR38 toolkit. This rendered view allows the wearer of the HMD to see the whole 360 view from the position of the camera by looking around. Because the content is video and the camera is stationary, the viewer cannot zoom, but only pan and tilt to see the complete 360° view. Spherical Display In an effort to provide a spherical projection that could be viewed by more than one person, useful for on-set review and monitoring of captured content, we support and also use a Pufferfish spherical display39 by Pufferfish, Ltd. of Edinburgh for our realtime streaming demonstration at SIGGRAPH 2016 as shown in Fig. 3. The Pufferfish display provides a rear projection inside a translucent sphere.
